strongest_objection: Changing the founder could make the earlier receipt and the later birth change together, even if the later rule never uses what the enrolled knot retained.
response: Cross the two independent donor diversions, hold the partner’s earlier payment fixed, inspect all real witnesses and competing parent groups, retain all funded alternatives and permute every donor binding. Change a separate earlier payment at fixed partner choice, and require matching locally visible values before claiming complete local ambiguity. Scope identical-founder invariance to birth rosters and grants.
advisor_verdict: The strongest objection is that changing the founder could make the earlier receipt and the later birth change together, even if the later rule never uses what the enrolled knot retained. The design can distinguish those explanations. It fixes the other enrolled payer’s earlier donor payment where possible, traces both distinct payments to any claimed common older holder, checks larger competing groups, and requires an alternative funded birth when the target is absent. A positive causal finding requires the ordinary rule to use that retained coholding. A change in the knot’s own count alone would establish a readable sign of the earlier event. The donor-slot permutations test whether a particular distinction matters or any payment from that donor serves. In the balanced comparison, equal counts settle what counting can reveal. A claim about the knot’s entire anonymous holding also requires matching its locally visible values. For identical founders, the design distinguishes the roster and grants from the recipient of a particular tagged payment. These limits leave both positive and negative results reportable. This decision covers the prospective design only.
